results.title: India Song
results.brief_description:
In the 1930s, Anne-Marie Stratter lives in Calcutta with her husband, the French Ambassador. During a reception at the Embassy, Anne-Marie dances with her lover, Michael Richardson, unaware of her husband’s glances. Anne-Marie is equally unaware of the passion in the vice-consul’s eyes. The vice-consul declares is passion to Anne-Marie. She rebuffs him. The vice-consul runs off and a heartrending cry tears the stillness of the night. Further viweing: In ‘Son nom de Venise dans Calcutta desert’(1976), Marguerite Duras re-uses the same soundtrack, this time accompanied with images of the Embassy, now deserted, where the action of ‘India Song’ took place. The closing sequence of ‘Son nom de Venise dans Calcutta desert’ is used as the opening sequence for ‘India Song’.

Credits: Producer, Stephane Tchalgadjieff ; director, Marguerite Duras ; writer, Marguerite Duras ; photography, Bruno Nuytten ; music, Ludwig van Beethoven, Carlos d’Alessio.
Cast: Delphine Seyrig, Michel Lonsdale, Claude Mann, Mathieu Carriere, Didier Flamand, Vernon Dobtcheff.

results.title: Ma Femme Est Formidable = My Wife Is Wonderful
results.brief_description:
Condemned without evidence as a ‘rake’ by his dimwitted wife Sylvia and his monstrous in-laws, Raymond Corbier is further bedeviled by the unwarranted advances of man-chasing Marguerite Rival.

Credits: Producer, Paul Cadeac ; director, Andre Hunebelle ; writer, Jean Halain ; photography, Paul Cotteret ; music, Jean Marion ; costumes, Pierre Balmain.
Cast: Sophie Desmarets, Fernand Gravey, Simone Valere, Alfred Adam, Jacques Dynam, Max Dalban, Pauline Carton, Suzanne Dehelly.

results.title: Les Chouans = the Royalists
results.brief_description:
Marquis de Montauran has been chosen to lead ‘les Chouans’ (the army formed by the inhabitants of the western provinces of France opposed to the Revolutionary government). But he falls in love with a spy working for the republican government, the very beautiful Marie de Verneuil.

Credits: Producer, Georges Legrand ; director, Henri Calef ; writer, Charles Spaak, Pierre Brive ; photography, Claude Renoir ; music, Joseph Kosma.
Cast: Jean Marais, Madeleine Robinson, Madeleine Lebeau, Marcel Herrand, Pierre Dux, Louis Seigner, Jacques Charron, Armontel.

results.title: Le Desordre a Vingt Ans = Disorder Is Twenty Years Old
results.brief_description:
In this documentary, Jacques Baratier compares life in the St Germain des Pres area of Paris in the the post WWII years and 20 years later in the Sixties (pre May 68). Rare documents and seldom seen footage of personalities, “overexposed films shot in obscure places” such as ‘Le Tabou’ recreate the ambiance of the great existentialist era. The interviewees recall the social changes that led to the movement. They include: Boris Vian, Alain Vian, Roger Blin, Juliette Greco, Raymond Queneau, Jean Cau, Simone de Beauvoir, Jean-Paul Sartre, Sophie Desmarets, Jean Cocteau, Roger Pierre, Arthur Adamov, Cesar, Anne-Marie Cazalis, Michel de Re, Roger Vadim, Annabel, Gabriel Pomerand, Sydney Bechet, Claude Luter etc… This film is followed by ‘Voila l’ordre’.

Credits: Director, Jacques Baratier.

results.title: Benito Cereno
results.brief_description:
In 1799, the Santo Domingo is sailing to Peru, when a slave mutiny erupts on board. Only seven crew members survive, including the Captain, Benito Cereno. The leader of the mutiny, Atimbo, wants to sail back to Africa. When the ship encounters troubles, an American vessel comes to the rescue. Cereno explains that his crew has taken ill with scurvy, including the human cargo imported from Africa. The slaves are down to only a few healthy men and Cereno is awaiting the right

Credits: Director, Serge Roullet ; writer, Serge Roullet ; photography, Ricardo Arronovitch.
Cast: Ruy Guerra, Georges Selmark, Temour Diop, Jacques Mercier, John Turner, Serge Roullet, Philippe Noury.

results.title: Le Vieil Homme et L' Enfant = the Old Man and the Boy
results.brief_description:
During the nazi occupation of Paris, an irrepressible eight-year old jewish boy, Claude, is sent to stay with an elderly couple in the country. Since Pepe, the old man, is a rabid anti-semite, the boy is instructed to conceal his origins. Once there, Claude and Pepe forge a close relationship - beautifully realized in the playing - in which the boy is amused by the old man’s bigoted outburst and delights in provoking him, while Pepe comes to dote on the child. Berri’s film is a reconstruction of his own childhood experience and he describes it as a ‘love affair between a Jew and an anti-Semite’. Awards: Berlin Film Festival (1967): Best Actor for Michel Simon.

Credits: Director, Claude Berri ; writers, Gerard Brach, Claude Berri ; photography, Jean Penzer ; music, Georges Delerue.
Cast: Michel Simon, Alain Cohen, Charles Denner, Luce Fabiole, Roger Carel, Paul Preboist, Zorica Lozice.

results.title: Le Vieux Fusil = the Old Gun
results.brief_description:
In Montauban in 1944, Julien Dandieu works as a surgeon in the local hospital. Frightened by the German army entering Montauban, he asks his friend Francois to drive his wife and daughter to a back country village where Julien owns an old castle. One week later, Julien decides to go and join his family for the week end, but the Germans are already occupying the village. On his way to the house, Julien discovers the corpses of the villagers in the church, then, further away, the charred bodies of his daughter and his wife. He vows to personally kill every one of the Germans responsible in order to assuage his grief. Awards: French Academy of Cinema (Cesar) 1975: Best actor for Philippe Noiret ; Best film for Robert Enrico ; Best music for Francois de Roubaix.

Credits: Producer, Pierre Caro ; director, Robert Enrico ; writer, Robert Enrico, Pascal Jardin, Claude Vieillot ; photography, Etienne Becker ; music, Francois de roubaix.
Cast: Romy Schneider, Philippe Noiret, Jean Bouise, Madeleine Ozeray, Catherine Delaporte.

results.title: Classe Tous Risques = the Big Risk
results.creator_credit: Claude Sautet, Jacques Plante, Jean Darvey and Robert Amon
results.brief_description:
Abel Davos is on the most wanted list in both France and Italy. With the assistance of Naldi, he manages to reunite with Therese, his wife, and their children in the border town of Vintimillle. As they make their way to Menton, the police attempt to arrest them. The operation takes a nasty turn and both Therese and Naldi are killed. Abel and the children go into hiding in Nice where Abel endeavours to re-establish contact with former accomplices and organise a bank robbery.

Credits: Producers, Jean Darvey, Robert Amon, Jacques Plante ; director, Claude Sautet ; writers, Claude Sautet, Pascal Jardin, Jose Giovanni ; photography, Ghislain Cloquet ; music, Georges Delerue.
Cast: Lino Ventura, Jean-Paul Belmondo, Sandra Milo, Jacques Dacqmine, Marcel Dalio, Bernard Dheran, Claude Cerval, Michel Ardan, Rene Genin, Charles Blavette.

results.title: Glissements Progressifs du Plaisir = Successive Slidings Of Pleasure
results.creator_credit: Alain Robbe-Grillet, Andre Cohen, Henri Boublil and Marcel Sebaoun
results.brief_description:
Alice has been placed in custody in a juvenile detention centre run by nuns. She is accused of the murder of her flatmate who has been found tied up in bed, a pair of scissors in the heart. During questioning, Alice rants and raves, expressing all sorts of fantasies. Shocked at first, her lawyer becomes slowly fascinated by Alice’s behaviour and enters in a series of lesbian sex plays with her client.

Credits: Producers, Henri Boublil, Andre Cohen, Marcel Sebaoun ; director, Alain Robbe-Grillet ; writer, Alain Robbe-Grillet ; photography, Yves Lafaye ; music, Michel Fano ; assistant director, Luc Beraud.
Cast: Anicee Alvina, Olga Georges-Picot, Jean-Louis Trintignant, Michel Lonsdale, Jean Martin, Maxence Mailfort, Isabelle Huppert, Bob Wade.

results.title: Clair de Femme = Woman Light
results.brief_description:
Michel is running away from home and his dying wife. While wandering aimlesslely, he meets Lydia who is still grieving the loss of her husband and child. For a whole night these two desperate characters are walking the streets of Paris, visiting bars and cabarets, and meeting equally strange, emotionally displaced people.

Credits: Producer, Georges-Alain Vuille ; director, Costa-Gavras ; writer, Costa-Gavras ; photography, Ricardo Aronovich ; music, Jean Musy.
Cast: Yves Montand, Romy Schneider, Romolo Valli, Lila Kedrova, Heinz Bennent, Roberto Benigni, Francois Perrot, Daniel Mesguich, Catherine Allegret, Dieter Schidor.
